properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 28 at 4:24AM EDT until September 28 at 10:30AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Monmouth County in central New Jersey...
Northeastern Ocean County in southern New Jersey...

* WHEN...Until 1030 AM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 423 AM EDT, gauge reports rising river levels due to excess
runoff. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the
warned area. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain have fallen over the
last three days.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Allenwood.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 28 at 9:13AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor remains within Minor Flood Stage due to
tidal effects. River levels are forecast to gradually subside through
Minor Flood Stage this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Monday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Monday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.6 feet today, and then gradually subside through Minor
Flood Stage this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.6
feet on 10/14/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island Louisiana out 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 28 at 7:56AM CDT until September 28 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
SMWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island
Louisiana out 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 900 AM CDT.

* At 756 AM CDT, a strong thunderstorm was located over open waters
of Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island
Louisiana out 20 to 60 NM zone, moving southeast at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island
Louisiana out 20 to 60 NM.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 28 at 7:55AM EDT until September 28 at 1:45PM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by prolonged heavy rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Worcester County in central Massachusetts...
Southern Norfolk County in eastern Massachusetts...
Northwestern Bristol County in southeastern Massachusetts...
West Central Plymouth County in southeastern Massachusetts...
Northeastern Providence County in Rhode Island...

* WHEN...Until 145 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from previous rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 747 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated continued light to at
times moderate rain falling over the warned area. Between 3 and 6
inches of rain have fallen over the last 48 hours in the warned
area. Additional rainfall expected through this morning could
lead to areas of street and poor drainage flooding. The
Blackstone River above Woonsocket is now in minor flood stage
levels at 11.96 ft, which leads to low- lying flooding along
portions of Cumberland and Woonsocket as well as off of Route 122
in Cumberland.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Brockton, Pawtucket, Taunton, East Providence, Woonsocket,
Cumberland, Randolph, North Providence, Franklin, North
Attleborough, Norwood, Stoughton, Attleboro, Walpole and
Mansfield.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.
